concepts.def: Processes instructions via the fetch–decode–execute cycle.
Stores data and instructions in the same memory.
RAM is volatile working memory; ROM is permanent.
Fast memory close to the CPU for frequently used data.
Tiny, fast stores inside the CPU (e.g. the accumulator).
How many cycles the CPU performs per second.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Computers — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computers brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computers.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: RAM is described as volatile because:
options: Its contents are lost when the power is switched off
It catches fire easily
It cannot be read quickly
It stores data permanently
Programs and files must be kept permanently even when the power is off
RAM is too fast for most programs
The CPU cannot work without a DVD drive
It makes the screen brighter

mcqs.q: Which of these is a function of the operating system?
options: Managing memory, files and running programs
Physically cooling the processor
Generating electricity for the computer
Printing without a printer
A solid-state drive
The operating system
A web browser
A device driver

mcqs.q: Does adding more RAM let you permanently store more files?
options: Yes - RAM and hard drive space are the same thing.
Yes - more RAM means more space to save documents and photos.
No - RAM is volatile working memory; files are stored permanently on secondary storage, so more RAM helps run more programs at once, not store more files.
Yes - ROM is just a bigger version of RAM.

mcqs.q: Is the CPU the whole computer case (tower)?
options: No - the CPU is a single chip on the motherboard inside the case; the tower also contains memory, storage, the power supply and other components.
Yes - RAM and hard drive space are the same thing.
Yes - CPU stands for Computer Packaging Unit.
Yes - the box on the desk is called the CPU.

mcqs.q: Is ROM where the programs you install are stored?
options: Yes - ROM is just a bigger version of RAM.
Yes - apps are saved into ROM when you install them.
Yes - RAM and hard drive space are the same thing.
No - installed programs go on secondary storage; ROM holds the fixed start-up (boot) instructions written by the manufacturer.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “RAM”?
options: Volatile main memory holding the programs and data currently in use; its contents are lost when the power is switched off.
The component that executes program instructions by repeatedly fetching them from memory, decoding them and carrying them out.
The physical parts of a computer system, such as the processor, memory chips, storage drives, keyboard and screen.
Non-volatile storage such as magnetic hard disks, solid-state drives and optical discs, which keeps programs and files when the power is off.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Operating system”?
options: System software that manages the hardware, memory, files, security and running programs, and provides the user interface.
The physical parts of a computer system, such as the processor, memory chips, storage drives, keyboard and screen.
Non-volatile storage such as magnetic hard disks, solid-state drives and optical discs, which keeps programs and files when the power is off.
The component that executes program instructions by repeatedly fetching them from memory, decoding them and carrying them out.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Central processing unit (CPU)”?
options: System software that manages the hardware, memory, files, security and running programs, and provides the user interface.
The component that executes program instructions by repeatedly fetching them from memory, decoding them and carrying them out.
The programs that run on a computer, including the operating system and applications, made of instructions the hardware executes.
Non-volatile storage such as magnetic hard disks, solid-state drives and optical discs, which keeps programs and files when the power is off.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Software”?
options: Volatile main memory holding the programs and data currently in use; its contents are lost when the power is switched off.
The programs that run on a computer, including the operating system and applications, made of instructions the hardware executes.
The physical parts of a computer system, such as the processor, memory chips, storage drives, keyboard and screen.
Non-volatile storage such as magnetic hard disks, solid-state drives and optical discs, which keeps programs and files when the power is off.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Secondary storage”?
options: The programs that run on a computer, including the operating system and applications, made of instructions the hardware executes.
The component that executes program instructions by repeatedly fetching them from memory, decoding them and carrying them out.
Non-volatile storage such as magnetic hard disks, solid-state drives and optical discs, which keeps programs and files when the power is off.
The physical parts of a computer system, such as the processor, memory chips, storage drives, keyboard and screen.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hardware”?
options: Volatile main memory holding the programs and data currently in use; its contents are lost when the power is switched off.
The programs that run on a computer, including the operating system and applications, made of instructions the hardware executes.
The component that executes program instructions by repeatedly fetching them from memory, decoding them and carrying them out.
The physical parts of a computer system, such as the processor, memory chips, storage drives, keyboard and screen.

mcqs.q: A hard drive holds 2 TB. Using 1 TB = 1000 GB, how many gigabytes is that?
options: 20 GB
200 GB

Small, fast memory next to the processor
Magnetic storage with moving parts — slowest here
